subject: Re: IP infringement notice and indemnity — scope & fallback
messages:
From: Elena Torres <legal@novaprod.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: IP infringement notice — sample outputs attached

Logan / Redwood team,

We detected alleged third-party IP in outputs generated by an endpoint on your platform that we use (project: "NovaBot"). Per section 7.3 of the draft MSA, NovaProd is providing formal notice and requesting defense/indemnity for the claim from the downstream complainant (attached). We are including the technical samples and timestamps so your engineering team can reproduce.

Summary:
- Claim received from BetaSoft, alleges novel algorithm replication in model outputs dated 2026-07-28 to 2026-08-02.
- Samples in evidence-samples.zip (sha256 listed in the PDF).
- We consider this a triggered third-party IP claim under the current order form because the outputs were generated via your hosted runtime.

Immediate asks:
1) Confirm receipt and the Redwood contact for legal + engineering investigations by EOD PDT.
2) Provide any logs/trace IDs you will need (we included timestamps and user IDs in the PDF).
3) Let us know your proposed mutual action plan and expected timeline for acknowledgement to the complainant.

Attachments: NovaProd_IP_Claim_Notice.pdf, evidence-samples.zip

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Senior Counsel, NovaProd, Inc.
elena.torres@novaprod.com
Phone: +1 415 555 0192

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <legal@novaprod.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 19:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: IP infringement notice — sample outputs attached

Elena — thanks for the heads up and for the detailed package. I confirm receipt.

Short answer to your asks:
- Redwood legal + engineering triage team confirmed: Kimberly Park (legal) and Rishi Malhotra (acct lead / escalation) are on copy and will coordinate.
- Engineering will need the trace IDs you included; we'll request any missing logs via secure upload link.
- Proposed timeline: 24h acknowledgement to complainant with offer to coordinate on reproducing examples; technical triage report within 72h; draft mutual action plan and redline exchange within 5 business days.

Next steps from our side (today):
- Kimberly will review the notice and produce a redline of the order form indemnity paragraph that reflects our standard carveouts for model-generated outputs and training data.
- Engineering will start reproduction and we'll share a minimized bundle of logs.

Can you confirm if NovaProd expects immediate takedown of the model/deployment while the investigation proceeds, or if containment (rate-limit, disable public routes) is sufficient? That changes the mitigations we propose to the complainant.

I will also upload the claim materials into the internal incident tracker and share a link.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com

From: Elena Torres <legal@novaprod.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Novaprod Tech Ops <it@novaprod.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: IP infringement notice — sample outputs attached

Logan — appreciate the fast turnaround.

For mitigation: NovaProd prefers containment over full takedown at this stage. Specifically:
- Please suspend the public endpoint that produced the flagged outputs and enable a read-only, internal-only mode for NovaProd engineers (we will coordinate access).
- We will not publish the complainant's materials while we investigate; aim is to limit further exposure.

We've also uploaded additional logs to the secure folder and added a short writeup from our product team describing how NovaBot queries are constructed (link inside the PDF). We can accept a 72h triage window before contacting the complainant with a joint status update.

From our side: we expect Redwood to confirm whether indemnity will be handled under the current order form, and if not, propose concrete redlines. Our counsel is available for a quick call tomorrow morning PST to align.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <legal@novaprod.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: IP infringement notice — draft redline and proposal

Elena — thanks for the clarification and for uploading the additional logs. I reviewed NovaProd_IP_Claim_Notice.pdf and the evidence bundle. I've attached a proposed redline of the Order Form (RW-redline-orderform-20260811.docx) with the following high-level points: 

Key legal positions (summary):
- Redwood is willing to accept defense/indemnity for third-party IP claims to the extent the claim arises from our hosted runtime operations and not from (a) customer-supplied training data, or (b) customer prompt injection/obviously malicious inputs.
- We propose a carveout for model outputs that are substantially identical to a customer-supplied copyrighted corpus (i.e., direct replica of provided training artifacts) — in that scenario liability would be allocated to the customer.
- Limitations: propose a per-claim monetary cap tied to the order form value (two times the annual committed spend) and an overall aggregate cap aligned to standard carrier limits.
- Insurance/offset: we propose an insurance-first approach. If NovaProd has primary insurance that covers the claim, Redwood's indemnity would be reduced by any amounts recovered from that insurance (insurance offset).
- Evidence / cooperation: require complainant to provide the original materials, signed affidavit from the IP owner and a clear mapping showing the alleged overlap. We included precise SLA windows for evidence delivery and remediation timelines.

Operational asks for triage & mitigation:
- Redwood engineering asks for a copy of the production trace IDs and a short reproducible prompt set; we've provided a secure upload link where we will post repro logs.
- Proposed interim containment: Redwood can suspend the public endpoint for NovaProd and enable an internal-only read mode for your engineers (per Elena's ask).

If NovaProd accepts the carveouts and the proposed cap/insurance language, we can issue a single combined redline exchange and then sign — this avoids repeated back-and-forth on narrow phrasing. If NovaProd cannot accept the insurance-offset or cap levels, please indicate priority (cap vs carveouts vs proof threshold) so we can table lower-priority items.

Attachments: RW-redline-orderform-20260811.docx

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <legal@novaprod.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:43:00 +0000
Subject: Re: IP infringement notice — commercial proposal and next steps

Elena / team — looping on the commercial tradeoffs to make this practical for both sides. Quick commercial summary from Redwood sales: 

1) We are prepared to accept the indemnity mechanism outlined by Kimberly (insurance-first, per-claim cap) as our starting point, provided NovaProd agrees to: 
   - Confirm that the endpoint will be placed in internal-only mode during the 72h triage window; and
   - Accept a short-term SLA credit structure (credits applied to committed spend) rather than immediate increases to the liability cap while provenance is investigated.

2) Canary fallback: to avoid production disruption for NovaProd customers, we can offer an automatic routing policy — if a claim pattern is detected we can route NovaProd traffic to a stricter model variant (quantized / safety-filtered) for 48–96 hours while we finish the triage. That provides immediate containment without forcing a hard takedown.

3) Timing / next steps: if NovaProd can confirm the containment approach and accept insurance-offset language in principle, Kimberly and I will finalize a short combined amendment (order form appendix) and circulate for countersignature. We can also open a single shared DocuSign envelope to accelerate execution.

Please confirm which of the following you prefer (reply with A, B, or C):
A) Internal-only access + canary fallback + SLA credits (fastest)
B) Full endpoint suspension + insist on higher cap (slower; requires procurement sign-off)
C) We continue redline negotiation with both options on the table (need 5 business days)

If A, we'll draft and target execution by end of week.

Thanks — available for a quick call if helpful.

Rishi Malhotra
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Phone: +1 650 555 0224
